site_or_subject: Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island Unit 1) restart for Microsoft
record: NRC reactor page (docket 05000289, read 2026-10-24): its decommissioning table gives permanent shutdown on 2019-09-20 and fuel removed on 2019-09-26, while its text says the unit 'permanently ceased operations on September 26, 2019'; licence status SAFSTOR; the name change to the Christopher M. Crane Clean Energy Center was approved by Amendment No. 306 (2025-05-13); the request to revise the operating licence and technical specifications was submitted 2025-07-31 and accepted 2025-09-04; the NRC issued a draft EA and draft FONSI on 2026-06-03 and the final EA and FONSI on 2026-09-18, concluding no EIS was needed; the page lists a request for additional information on the operating licence request dated 2026-09-25, and restart had not been authorised. NRC letter ML26266A106 (2026-09-24) gives notice of the final EA. Water: the Susquehanna River Basin Commission approved on 2026-06-04 (Docket No. 20221203) surface water withdrawal of up to 73.200 mgd (peak day) and consumptive use of up to 21.000 mgd (peak day). The SRBC fact sheet gives the earlier approvals: power generation (Docket No. 20110610) 122.8 mgd withdrawal and 19.2 mgd consumptive use; decommissioning 44 mgd and 6 mgd. Grid: FERC on 2026-06-01 granted a one-time waiver allowing 760 MW of capacity interconnection rights to move from the Eddystone units to Crane [press: World Nuclear News; the FERC order, eLibrary accession 20260601-3068, could not be read]. Loan: DOE's Loan Programs Office closed a USD 1 billion loan to Constellation Energy Generation, LLC to help finance the Crane Clean Energy Center (DOE release, 2025-11-18). Spent fuel: see us-nuclear-deal-plants-spent-fuel.
